articleTitle: Essential CADMAT-an integrated approach to a foundation course for electronic engineering undergraduates
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electronic CADMAT in Teaching
abstract: The advent of industrial CAD for educational use has encouraged staff of Manchester University to explore the use of such software in the teaching of both analogue and digital circuit design and an increasing proportion of available electronic CAD has been incorporated in the core teaching. Then following success with a bid in response to the ESPRIT action on VLSI skills, the increased resources have enabled the establishment of a new degree course entitled Electronic Systems Engineering (ESE). So it was that a first year laboratory course in CADMAT was initiated. The strategy of placing the CADMAT laboratory in the first year of the degree course is to instil at the outset the importance of advanced CAD in achieving the correct design and manufacture of an electronic system of substantial complexity. This paper presents details of the first-year CADMAT programme, the laboratory supervision arrangements and of the criteria used in assessment. In addition, an appraisal is made of its success in providing a foundation on which to build subsequent years of the ESE degree course.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electronic CADMAT in Teaching
abstract: Nibbler is a simple microprocessor designed as the basis of a third year undergraduate VLSI fabrication project. Nibbler is not a high performance processor-wherever possible the hardware has been simplified to reduce the opportunity for design errors. The resulting design requires about 2-3,000 transistors for a CMOS full custom implementation. A cross-assembler and behavioural simulator are available. Approximately 30 undergraduates take the VLSI design course annually. In 1990 about two-thirds of the projects have been based on the Nibbler architecture implemented using three different toolsets and various design strategies. Teams of up to six students have collaborated in the larger projects in an attempt to simulate industrial working practices.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electronic CADMAT in Teaching
abstract: There is a requirement to disseminate the capabilities of computer-aided design (CAD) and computer-based simulation (CBS) to undergraduate power engineers in an apposite and academically acceptable fashion, but there are few immediately suitable software packages. This paper considers the necessity for, and discusses the application of, CAD and CBS in undergraduate teaching in Energy Systems in the Department of Electrical Engineering in the University of Edinburgh.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improving on the use of industrial CAD and simulation packages in teaching automation and robotics
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electronic CADMAT in Teaching
abstract: Robotics is the most powerful tool available to ensure the success of modern manufacturing industry in Europe. The requirement for education and training in the area of robotics led to the choice of name for a new course at Portsmouth Polytechnic; Automation and Robotics. The course consists of both practical and theoretical work. The practical work is in three parts, beginning with basic control techniques. The other two parts are an investigation into the use of sensors and transducers in a flexible manufacturing environment (especially vision systems) and path and trajectory planning and the control of industrial robots.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Synthesis of op-amp based active-RC networks using a parallel path approach
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electronic CADMAT in Teaching
abstract: Parallel-path op-amp based networks have been used in the design of active-RC and active-R oscillators. The relative ease with which this technique can be employed to synthesize second- and higher-order transfer functions using first-order building blocks has led the author to develop a series of engineering tasks of varying length and complexity suitable for presentation to second year honours undergraduates. Students are expected to carry out the initial design work by hand calculations using simple op amp models. They are then expected to verify the performances of their circuits and to compare them with those of more established designs using PSPICE simulation. It is also intended to verify the performances of some of the designs in the laboratory in future years.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The integration of CAD into power electronics courses
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electronic CADMAT in Teaching
abstract: The Power Electronics option in the final year of the BEng degree at Manchester Polytechnic is concerned with the terminal characteristics of switching devices and the circuits in which these devices operate to transform power from one sort to another. Several CAD packages are used (both industry standard and custom designed) but the paper concentrates on the use of PSPICE as a means of enhancing the teaching/learning process and as a tool in the design of power switching circuits. Students use PSPICE UC as an aid to understanding the operation of thyristor converter circuits and to determine the transient performance of dc machines (including mechanical effects).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
